column1: # This is a TEST FIXTURE, not a working requirements file. The checks
# rebuild it into a workbook in memory (check_support.workbook_from_tsv)
# because requirements_io reads .xlsx and nothing else.
# It exists to exercise PER-CATEGORY PASSING GRADES, which the BSc fixture
# cannot: a BSc refuses a D everywhere, so it needs no Pass column at all and
# every bar in it is the default C.
# A BA is different. A D earns credit toward the degree, but not in the major
# — not in a MATH or STAT category. So the file sets its default to D and
# overrides the eight major categories back to C.
# Written that way round on purpose. It mirrors the regulation's own shape
# ("D counts, except in the major"), and it fails safe: a category added here
# later inherits D, which is right for the electives that make up most of the
# degree. Default-C with D written on the electives would need fewer cells but
# would silently make each new elective category too strict.
# Section headings in [brackets]; blank lines and #-comments ignored.
